children: New Delhi, Sept. 25 -- A chemical stock, Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals (GNFC), has been enjoying healthy buying interest this year despite weak stock market sentiment. GNFC share price ended 0.78% higher at Rs.629.95 after hitting a 52-week high of Rs. 635.85 during the session on the BSE on Friday, 25 September, extending gains for the fourth consecutive session. In these four sessions, the stock has gained nearly 7%.

According to BSE data, the stock has surged 58% in the last six months, while equity benchmark Sensex has declined 2% in the same period. Year-to-date, the stock is up 28% compared to a 13% fall in the Sensex.

Brokerage firm Ventura expects the stock to rise further. It has a target price of Rs.810, implying 28.6% upside from the stock's closing price on 25 September on the BSE. It has a stop-loss of Rs.528 on the stock.

The brokerage firm underscored that the stock commenced its downtrend from the June 2024 high of Rs.776.60, breaching the 200 SMA and thereafter, traded below the averages, marking a low of Rs.365 hit in March 2026.

"During the correction phase, the stock slipped from Rs.776.60 and formed lower lows, reaching a low of Rs.365. Later, buying emerged and the stock commenced its up move reaching a high of Rs.616 in June 2026, but faced resistance in that area and entered into a consolidation zone trading around the short-term averages," said Ventura.

"Recently, after forming higher bottoms at Rs.528.80, the stock gave a symmetrical triangle breakout supported by volume reaching a high of Rs.635.85, which is higher than the previous swing highs. MACD, Williams Per cent Range, advance-decline, and Aroon indicators signal a positive crossover. The stock is trading above 200 SMA," Ventura said.

"Target of Rs.810 is expected with lower support levels at Rs.604, Rs.587, Rs.575, Rs.564, and Rs.548 in case of intermediate fall. A stop loss at Rs.528 is to be followed for the trade," said the brokerage firm.
In an exchange filing on 22 September, the company said that SES ESG Research Private
Limited had, on 21 September, assigned an environmental, social, and governance (ESG) score (adjusted) of "67 (grade B): Medium risk," for the company based on FY26 data.
According to the company, the latest rating reflects an improvement of 0.8 points in the ESG score compared to FY25, demonstrating its continued commitment to enhancing its ESG performance.
In another exchange filing on 23 September, the company said CRISIL ESG Ratings & Analytics Limited had assigned it an ESG rating of "CRISIL ESG 55" under the adequate category.
